moments.title: Eugene Williams drowns off 29th St
moments.text: During a heat wave, 17-year-old Eugene Williams drifted on a raft across an unofficial color line between the beaches used by Black and white swimmers. A white man threw rocks at him, and he drowned.

moments.title: A week of violence
moments.text: When police would not arrest the man Black witnesses named, fighting spread from the beach into the South Side. The state militia helped end the riot on Aug 3.

moments.title: The Negro in Chicago report
moments.text: A state commission of six Black and six white members published a 672-page study of the riot and of discrimination in housing, jobs and policing. Few of its 59 recommendations were carried out.

moments.title: A memorial plaque near the beach
moments.text: Students from York High School in Elmhurst and the Chicago Park District placed a marker for Eugene Williams and all the riot's victims near 29th St beach.

moments.title: The centennial
moments.text: On the riot's 100th anniversary, Chicago groups held commemorations; it was the first time the City of Chicago officially marked the riot.

moments.title: Today: markers for all 38 victims
moments.text: The Chicago Race Riot of 1919 Commemoration Project has installed markers at or near the places where each of the 38 people killed lost their lives.

facts.label: Killed
facts.note: 23 Black and 15 white people. Some accounts at the time claimed more.

facts.label: Injured
facts.note: Britannica and Wikipedia give 537; the NEH cites about 520.

sources.title: The Negro in Chicago, 1922 (Newberry Library, Chicago 1919: Confronting the Race Riots)
The Race Riot of 1919 (Chicago Race Riot of 1919 Commemoration Project)

checked.notes: Dates (July 27 to Aug 3, 1919), 38 killed (23 Black, 15 white) and more than 500 injured confirmed (Newberry Library, Britannica, Wikipedia). Injury counts range from about 520 to 537, so 'more than 500' stays. Sources disagree on the exact beaches (25th, 26th, 27th or 29th St); the pin stays near the 29th St beach. The 2009 plaque is listed on HMDB; the 2019 centennial was covered by WTTW; the project's 38 markers were reported complete in July 2026 (Axios, Chicago Sun-Times).
